Amazon’s growth requires leaders who move fast, have an entrepreneurial spirit to create new solutions, have an unrelenting tenacity to get things done, and are capable of breaking down and solving complex problems. The successful candidate will be a self-starter, comfortable with ambiguity and be able to create and maintain efficient & automated processes. They know and love working with data engineering tools, can model multidimensional datasets, and can partner effectively with business leaders to build the right data pipelines to answer key business questions. They will build efficient, flexible, extensible, and scalable data models, ETL designs and data integration services. They will also be required to support and manage growth of these data solutions. jobs.title: Data Engineer , Amazon Customer Service
jobs.description: Customer Experience Products (CXP) is part of Amazon's Customer Service (CS) organization, responsible for the data infrastructure that powers measurement, analytics, and automation across every customer service interaction — chat, voice, bots, and digital self-service. Our Data Engineers own the foundational data layer that BIEs, scientists, and product teams rely on to evaluate performance, shape OP planning, and drive customer-facing product improvements. You will join a team of data engineers, BIEs, and analysts who build and maintain the pipelines, schemas, and data platforms that underpin CXP's analytics ecosystem. The data you deliver directly shapes how Amazon understands and improves the customer service experience at scale — from customer journey funnels and resolver efficacy measurement to WBR automation and contact-reduction quantification. The team currently drives high-impact data engineering initiatives including migration to Gold Schema datasets, Datanet-to-Andes pipeline modernization, Panorama table consolidation, and cross-channel metrics unification. You will own meaningful data infrastructure workstreams from day one. Key job responsibilities - Design and implement logical and physical data models for complex, large-scale datasets that drive downstream analytics, WBR reporting, and self-service BI infrastructure across CXP verticals (CFS, CX-STAR, Concessions/CAP). - Build and optimize data pipelines (ETL/ELT) for difficult and large-scale datasets using technologies such as AWS Glue, Spark, Redshift, and EMR. Own pipeline reliability for business-critical reporting surfaces including VP-level dashboards and weekly business review decks. - Own data quality end-to-end. Establish SLAs, define data certification standards, build monitoring and alerting for pipeline health, and proactively identify and resolve data quality gaps (e.g., upstream DQ issues in Panorama tables, source data discrepancies). - Drive migration and modernization of data infrastructure. Lead migration of team-owned objects to dedicated schemas (e.g., Datanet-to-Andes migration), consolidate reporting tables to eliminate redundant queries, and align data sources to Gold Schema standards for consistent, auditable metrics. - Improve self-service access to data. Build tools and processes for data lineage tracking, discoverability, and governance. Reduce manual reporting overhead by engineering automated solutions that enable analysts and PMs to self-serve. - Partner cross-functionally with SDEs, BIEs, scientists, and PMs to understand data needs, propose solutions, and deliver datasets that enable stakeholders to make data-driven decisions. Integrate data solutions into broader team architecture and ensure alignment with CS Data & AI team dependencies. - Automate manual processes and improve operational excellence. Improve code quality, dependency management, and pipeline observability. Reduce BIE bandwidth consumed by manual data preparation work. - Mentor and develop peers. Participate in hiring, technical assessments, and code reviews. Raise the bar on data engineering practices across the team. A day in the life You might start your morning validating a pipeline migration that consolidates conversation and interaction ID attributes into a unified Panorama reporting table — eliminating the need for analysts to query multiple sources. After standup, you investigate a data quality gap in an upstream concessions table, root-cause the issue, and coordinate with the source team on a fix. In the afternoon, you build a new ETL job to power a customer journey funnel dataset that tracks the full path from CSHP entry through bot interaction to resolution. Before end of day, you review a teammate's pipeline code and help optimize a Spark job that's approaching its SLA window. We thrive on solving challenging data problems to build the infrastructure our customers — the analysts, scientists, and PMs who drive CS improvements — depend on every day. jobs.description: If you are interested in this position, please apply on Twitch's Career site https://www.twitch.tv/jobs/en/ About Us: Twitch is the world’s biggest live streaming service, with global communities built around gaming, entertainment, music, sports, cooking, and more. It is where thousands of communities come together for whatever, every day. We’re about community, inside and out. You’ll find coworkers who are eager to team up, collaborate, and smash (or elegantly solve) problems together. We’re on a quest to empower live communities, so if this sounds good to you, see what we’re up to on LinkedIn and X, and discover the projects we’re solving on our Blog. Be sure to explore our Interviewing Guide to learn how to ace our interview process. You can work from San Francisco, CA or Seattle, WA. About the Role Twitch is building the future of interactive entertainment. The Data Platform team develops and operates the data platform that powers data systems and decision-making. Our data pipeline receives over 200 billion events a day, and we forward live data to tens of systems as well as powering decisions at all levels of Twitch. This role is critical in developing and maintaining our enterprise-scale data processing systems that handle high-volume transactions while ensuring data security, privacy compliance, and optimal performance. You'll be part of a dynamic team that designs and implements comprehensive data solutions, from real-time processing architectures to secure storage solutions and privacy-compliant data access layers. The role involves close collaboration with cross-functional teams, including software development engineers, product managers and scientists, to create data products that power critical business capabilities. You'll have the opportunity to work with leading technologies in cloud computing, big data processing, and machine learning infrastructure, while contributing to the development of robust data governance frameworks. If you're passionate about solving complex technical challenges in high-scale environments, thrive in a collaborative team setting, and want to make a lasting impact on our organization's data infrastructure, this role offers an exciting opportunity to shape the future of our data and AI capabilities. Key job responsibilities - Design and implement ETL/ELT frameworks that handle large-scale data operations, while building reusable components for data ingestion, transformation, and orchestration while ensuring data quality and reliability. - Establish and maintain robust data governance standards by implementing comprehensive security controls, access management frameworks, and privacy-compliant architectures that safeguard sensitive information. - Drive the implementation of data solutions, both real-time and batch, optimizing them for both analytical workloads and AI/ML applications. - Lead technical design reviews and provide mentorship on data engineering best practices, identifying opportunities for architectural improvements and guiding the implementation of enhanced solutions. - Build data quality frameworks with robust monitoring systems and validation processes to ensure data accuracy and reliability throughout the data lifecycle. - Drive continuous improvement initiatives by evaluating and implementing new technologies and methodologies that enhance data infrastructure capabilities and operational efficiency. A day in the life The day often begins with a team huddle to align priorities, followed by a review of data pipeline monitoring alarms to address any processing issues and ensure data quality standards are maintained across systems. Throughout the day, you'll find yourself immersed in various technical tasks, including developing and optimizing ETL/ELT processes, implementing data governance controls, and reviewing code for data processing systems. You'll work closely with software engineers, scientists, and product managers, participating in technical design discussions and sharing your expertise in data architecture and engineering best practices. Your responsibilities extend to communicating with non-technical stakeholders, explaining data-related projects and their business impact. You'll also mentor junior engineers and contribute to maintaining comprehensive technical documentation. You'll troubleshoot issues that arise in the data infrastructure, optimize the performance of data pipelines, and ensure data security and compliance with relevant regulations. Staying updated on the latest data engineering technologies and best practices is crucial, as you'll be expected to incorporate new learnings into your work. By the end of a typical day, you'll have advanced key data infrastructure initiatives, solved complex technical challenges, and improved the reliability, efficiency, and security of data systems. Whether it's implementing new data governance controls, optimizing data processing workflows, or enhancing data platforms to support new AI models, your work directly impacts the organization's ability to leverage data for critical business decisions and AI capabilities. If you are not sure that every qualification on the list above describes you exactly, we'd still love to hear from you! At Amazon, we value people with unique backgrounds, experiences, and skillsets. If you’re passionate about this role and want to make an impact on a global scale, please apply! About the team The Data Intelligence team is a new function within Amazon Customer Service, a global, cross-functional organization of applied scientists, data scientists, economists, software engineers, data engineers, and technical product managers dedicated to advancing AI capabilities and creating meaningful impact for customers. We build data solutions and contextual intelligence using Generative AI, Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing, Ontology, Agentic AI, Multi-Agentic AI Architectures, Reinforcement Learning, Knowledge Graphs, and Model Context Protocol. We move with urgency, build for the long term, and prioritize getting customer experience right, because our work is only successful when it meaningfully improves outcomes for customers Internal job description - 3+ years of data engineering experience - 1+ years of developing and operating large-scale data structures for business intelligence analytics using ETL/ELT processes experience - 1+ years of developing and operating large-scale data structures for business intelligence analytics using OLAP technologies experience - 1+ years of developing and operating large-scale data structures for business intelligence analytics using SQL experience - 1+ years of developing and operating large-scale data structures for business intelligence analytics using Oracle experience - Experience with AWS technologies like Redshift, S3, AWS Glue, EMR, Kinesis, FireHose, Lambda, and IAM roles and permissions - Experience with non-relational databases / data stores (object storage, document or key-value stores, graph databases, column-family databases) - Experience with data modeling, warehousing and building ETL pipelines Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, AWS Payments & Fraud Prevention
jobs.description: What if the data you engineer could stop fraud before it happens - and protect millions of AWS customers worldwide? The Payments and Fraud Data Platform team within AWS Payments & Fraud is the backbone of one of the most critical missions at AWS: ensuring every transaction is safe, every suspension is justified, and every customer experience is seamless. We process petabytes of data daily, powering the ML models, rule engines, and real-time reporting systems that allow us to detect bad actors. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer who is passionate about building large-scale data systems, thrives in ambiguity, and wants to work at the intersection of big data, machine learning, non-payment and fraud prevention. Key job responsibilities Architect & Build Petabyte-Scale Data Pipelines - Design, develop, and optimize batch and near-real-time data pipelines using Amazon Managed Airflow (MWAA), Fargate, EMR, Apache Iceberg, and Amazon Redshift to ingest, transform, and serve data at massive scale. Power ML & Rules Engines - Deliver high-quality, timely datasets that fuel non payment and fraud detection ML models and business rule engines, directly impacting fraud prevention and non-payment suspension accuracy. Build Intelligent Data Access Layers - Design and implement a Smart Query & Data Access Analyzer that profiles query patterns, identifies hot data, and automatically promotes frequently accessed datasets into hot memory tiers (e.g., OpenSearch, DynamoDB DAX, Redshift RA3 caching) for sub-second retrieval. Create Natural Language SQL Interfaces - Leverage Amazon Bedrock and LLM (large language models) to build a natural language-to-SQL generation tool that empowers analysts and stakeholders to query complex fraud datasets conversationally - no SQL expertise required. Develop Real-Time Dashboards & Insights - Build rich, interactive dashboards using Grafana and internal tooling that provide real-time visibility into fraud trends, pipeline health, data quality metrics, and operational KPIs. Curate a Living Data Dictionary - Design and maintain a comprehensive, searchable data catalog and dictionary that provides rich metadata, lineage, and documentation - improving discoverability and self-service analytics across the organization. Champion Data Quality at Scale - Implement automated data validation, anomaly detection, and reconciliation frameworks that ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency across the entire data lifecycle. Secure & Govern Sensitive Data - Implement encryption, fine-grained access controls, audit trails, and compliance frameworks to protect highly sensitive payments and fraud data. Monitor, Optimize, Repeat - Build observability into everything , proactive alerting, pipeline performance tracking, SLA monitoring, and intelligent auto-remediation to ensure five-nines data reliability. About the team The AWS Payments & Fraud Prevention team protects AWS and its customers from fraud, abuse, and account compromise at global scale. We build highly scalable, batch and near real-time systems that ingest billions of signals daily, process petabytes of data, and make timed decisions to stop bad actors from account registration through the entire customer lifecycle. Our platform is built on a modern, cloud-native architecture designed for petabyte-class batch processing. Our stack includes Amazon MWAA orchestrates workflows, while EMR and Fargate handle scalable data processing. Amazon Redshift powers our data warehouse, complemented by an Apache Iceberg lakehouse for open table format flexibility. DynamoDB and OpenSearch drives search and analytics, and Amazon Bedrock serves as our AI/ML foundation. Development is accelerated with Kiro, an AI-powered IDE, and Grafana provides full-stack observability. We are a team of builders who care deeply about customer trust and love solving complex problems at massive scale. - 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience - 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience - 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience - 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience - 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience - Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field - Experience programming with at least one software programming language - 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience - Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner. The base salary range for this position is listed below. Your Amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs). Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. Amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, Basic Life & AD&D insurance and option for Supplemental life plans, EAP, Mental Health Support, Medical Advice Line, Flexible Spending Accounts, Adoption and Surrogacy Reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. Learn more about our benefits at https://amazon.jobs/en/benefits . USA, WA, Seattle - 143,700.00 - 194,400.00 USD annually

jobs.title: Data Engineer, Robotics Delivery and Packaging Innovation
jobs.description: Are you passionate about sustainability and waste reduction efforts across Amazon's global organization? Are you interested in building the data foundation that drives solutions balancing packaging and automation to increase speed, reduce cost, and ultimately delight our customers? The Robotics Delivery and Packaging Innovation team is looking for a Data Engineer to join us in building and maintaining the end-to-end data pipelines and infrastructure that power our analytics and business decisions. This is your opportunity to be a core part of the team that reduces waste for our business and our customers. In this role, you will design, build, and operate the data pipelines behind our "source of truth" data store and metrics for warehouse automation and customer packaging. You will develop robust, scalable ETL/ELT solutions that integrate large, complex data spanning many sources and data structures using AWS tools, enabling data-driven decisions on OEE, machine metrics, and product performance across our packaging automation, IB sortation, and other warehouse automation products. We are looking for a builder with deep SQL proficiency, strong Python skills, and knowledge of data modeling and warehousing best practices. You will apply rigorous data quality and data security practices, including validation, deduplication, PII handling, access controls, and monitoring, so that stakeholders can trust the data and sensitive operational data stays protected as it moves through our pipelines. You'll partner closely with Business Intelligence Engineers, Data Scientists, Product, and Operations to translate raw data into reliable, well-governed datasets and actionable insights. The ideal candidate thrives amid ambiguity, builds for the future while delivering today, and understands the importance of code development best practices. If you love hard problems with many solutions and a diverse, results-oriented environment, come join us! Key job responsibilities • Be hands-on with ETL/ELT to build and maintain reliable, scalable data pipelines using SQL, Python, and Spark that support automated reporting for warehouse automation and customer packaging • Interface with other technology teams to extract, transform, and load data from a wide variety of sources spanning warehouse automation and customer packaging • Implement data structures using best practices in data modeling, ETL/ELT processes, SQL, and Redshift, and manage our "source of truth" data stores • Implement best practices in batch and real-time data processing to make pipelines performant • Apply strong data quality practices (validation, deduplication, PII handling, drift detection, and monitoring) so consumers can trust the data • Build data security and access controls into the data infrastructure, protecting sensitive operational and performance data throughout its lifecycle • Model data and metadata for ad-hoc and pre-built reporting, and deliver high-quality datasets to support BIEs, Data Scientists, and customer reporting needs • Manage and optimize cloud computing resources on AWS to support data infrastructure • Use AI-assisted development tools (e.g., Amazon Q, Kiro) to accelerate pipeline development, SQL, and debugging, while validating generated output for correctness • Create extensible, easy-to-maintain designs with a long-term vision, laying groundwork to support future machine learning and GenAI use cases • Participate in strategic and tactical planning discussions A day in the life As a Data Engineer on this team, you will own the end-to-end data pipelines and infrastructure that serve as our "source of truth" for warehouse automation and customer packaging metrics. You will design, build, and operate robust and scalable ETL/ELT solutions, integrating complex data from dozens of sources to enable data-driven decisions across the Robotics Delivery and Packaging Innovation Organization. You will partner closely with Business Intelligence Engineers, Data Scientists, Software Engineers, Product Managers, and Operations teams to translate raw requirements into reliable and scalable data pipelines producing datasets that can be used and trusted across the org. You will also champion data quality and security practices, ensuring stakeholders can trust the data while sensitive operational information stays protected throughout its lifecycle. - 1+ years of data engineering experience - 2+ years of analyzing and interpreting data with Redshift, Oracle, NoSQL etc. experience - Bachelor's degree in a quantitative/technical field such as computer science, engineering, statistics - Knowledge of distributed systems as it pertains to data storage and computing - Experience with data modeling, warehousing and building ETL pipelines - Experience with one or more query language (e.g., SQL, PL/SQL, DDL, MDX, HiveQL, SparkSQL, Scala) - Experience with one or more scripting language (e.g., Python, KornShell) - Experience with big data technologies such as: Hadoop, Hive, Spark, EMR - Experience with any ETL tool like, Informatica, ODI, SSIS, BODI, Datastage, etc. Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. jobs.title: Data Engineer, Amazon Prime
jobs.description: Amazon Prime's Member Experience organization leads Research & Development for Amazon Prime. The program serves over 300 million members across 25 countries and is key to Amazon's customer growth and engagement. We build algorithms and systems for automated marketing, personalization, targeting, and decisioning using Artificial Intelligence and Economics. Within the engineering group, we develop world-class solutions to complex scientific and engineering problems at Amazon scale. You will work alongside world-class scientists to build a suite of fully automated, scalable, and robust products driven by the data systems you develop. As Prime expands its science-driven capabilities globally, we are growing the engineering team to meet increasing demand for reliable, high-throughput data infrastructure. Do you want to work with Amazon's best engineers on hard problems at massive scale? Do you want to impact over 300 million Prime members worldwide? Are you someone who likes using big data to drive high-impact business decisions? If so, come join our team! Key job responsibilities Build and maintain big data pipelines for machine learning applications at Amazon scale, ensuring stability and performance across terabyte-sized datasets Advance data engineering infrastructure using tools such as AWS Glue, Spark, Amazon EMR, and EMR Serverless to support science and analytics workloads Design and implement proactive data quality monitoring and alerting (e.g., anomaly detection) across production pipelines to safeguard downstream models Collaborate with scientists and analysts to create coherent data models and analysis-ready datasets that improve the customer experience for over 300 million members worldwide Evaluate and integrate generative AI tools where appropriate to automate data workflows and improve team productivity A day in the life You will collaborate closely with Prime business leaders, scientists (economists, research scientists, applied scientists), and engineering leaders to build data solutions. You will work with AWS technologies such as Amazon EMR, Amazon S3, AWS Glue, AWS Lambda, and Amazon DynamoDB to process terabyte-scale data and support real-time access and orchestration across multiple systems. Your work will directly enhance scientific models and data applications that shape the Prime member experience globally. You will also participate in code reviews, design discussions, and team planning alongside both technical and business stakeholders. About the team The Prime Member Experience engineering team sits at the intersection of large-scale engineering systems and applied science ,econometrics, machine learning, and AI delivering applications that reach over 300 million customers. Our team includes data engineers, software engineers, and scientists who partner closely to build and operate real-time science products. We are focused on enabling Prime Science adoption worldwide across Amazon, and the growing complexity of our real-time data products creates data engineering challenges that give you hands-on experience with problems the broader industry will face in the years ahead. - 3+ years of data engineering experience - Experience with data modeling, warehousing and building ETL pipelines - Experience as a data engineer or related specialty (e.g., software engineer, business intelligence engineer, data scientist) with a track record of manipulating, processing, and extracting value from large datasets - Knowledge of professional software engineering & best practices for full software development life cycle, including coding standards, software architectures, code reviews, source control management, continuous deployments, testing, and operational excellence - Experience in at least one modern scripting or programming language, such as Python, Java, Scala, or NodeJS - Experience with AWS technologies like Redshift, S3, AWS Glue, EMR, Kinesis, FireHose, Lambda, and IAM roles and permissions - Experience with non-relational databases / data stores (object storage, document or key-value stores, graph databases, column-family databases) - Experience building/operating highly available, distributed systems of data extraction, ingestion, and processing of large data sets Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, AWS Network Data Management and Research
jobs.description: The Data Management and Research (DMR) team in AWS Networking is looking for a Senior Software Development Engineer to set the technical direction for Mentat, our real-time network analytics engine, and the broader Data Exchange Services that partner teams across Networking depend on. Mentat is built on ClickHouse for petabyte-scale analytical storage and query, Kubernetes (EKS and self-managed clusters) for orchestration at fleet scale, and Grafana as the primary visualization and self-service query surface for our customers. In this role you will own the architecture of these systems, turn the hardest and most ambiguous multi-team problems into clear multi-quarter plans, and deliver them through other engineers. You will drive the reliability, performance, and cost strategy for ClickHouse clusters and their Kubernetes infrastructure across multiple regions, shape how teams consume data through Grafana, and raise the engineering bar through design, review, and mentorship. If you want senior IC leverage where your impact comes from architecture, judgment, and growing other engineers, and you want that work to shape how AWS Networking sees its own data, this is that role. Key job responsibilities As a Senior SDE on DMR, you set the technical direction for the platform and own the architecture of our most critical systems. You take the hardest, most ambiguous problems spanning multiple services and teams, turn them into clear multi-quarter plans, and deliver them through other engineers. You are a force multiplier: your designs, standards, and judgment raise the quality of everything the team ships, and your influence reaches well beyond DMR into partner and customer teams across Networking. This is a hands-on senior IC role where your leverage comes from architecture, direction setting, and developing other engineers rather than from individual output alone. A day in the life A typical day moves between deep technical work and org-level influence. You review and shape the architecture for a cross-service initiative such as the Mentat global rollout or long-term storage, then meet with partner teams across Alerts, SET, CET, and NetOS/NPD to align on dependencies and sequencing. You dive deep on a recurring operational risk, decide where the team should and should not invest, and make a durability or cost call that holds for the next several quarters. You mentor other engineers toward their next level, interview for senior roles, and represent DMR's technical strategy in broader Networking forums. Fridays are meeting-free, so you protect that time for architecture and writing. About the team DMR owns and operates the Data Exchange Services for AWS Networking. jobs.title: Data Engineer, Amazon Live Data Engineering, Sciences and Analytics (DESA)
jobs.description: Description Amazon Live is building the future of shoppable video — connecting brands with customers through livestreams, short-form video, and creator-driven content across Amazon Shopping, Fire TV, Prime Video, and social platforms. The product serves millions of monthly viewers, processes billions of events daily across 9 marketplaces, and generates tens of millions of dollars in advertiser revenue, with a goal to reach 100MM+ MAUs and 20K+ brands in the next couple of years. Amazon Live has a mature, high-performing data platform powering reporting across 9 marketplaces, 14+ dashboards, real-time creator analytics, and a growing suite of AI-native tooling (self-serve analytics agents, agentic operational assistants). The opportunity ahead is to build the next layer on that strong foundation: the team is standing up an intelligence layer — causal measurement, content intelligence, and ranking signals — and that requires a new class of foundational, reusable data assets purpose-built for both analytics and ML consumption. This role builds them. We are looking for a Data Engineer to join the DESA team as a dedicated owner of forward-looking data architecture. You will design and build durable, well-modeled datasets that serve three consumers at once: the BIE for executive reporting, the Applied Scientists for model training, and downstream ML systems (ranking, personalization, recommendations) for feature consumption. The goal is leverage — build an asset once, serve many use cases, and let the whole team move faster on top of it. Your work becomes the foundation the science function builds on: when the data assets are ready ahead of need, scientists model from day one instead of waiting on bespoke pipelines. This is a high-ownership role on a team that moves fast. You will go from problem to production quickly, in a challenging and fast-paced environment, and you will work across the full breadth of the data domain — platform engineering, data modeling, ML-ready feature production, data quality, and AI-assisted development. You will partner closely with Applied Scientists, MLEs, fellow Data Engineers, and the BIE, giving you the opportunity to learn and execute across every aspect of a modern data organization — from raw event ingestion through the models and reporting that move multi-million-dollar business decisions. Key job responsibilities - Design and build a content metadata layer that unifies broadcast events, product catalog data, creator profiles, and show metadata into reusable assets consumed by both dashboards and models. - Build cross-session shopper profile datasets that sessionize event data across visits and compute rolling engagement metrics (frequency, recency, depth, conversion lag). - Build integration pipelines connecting retail catalog and advertising performance data into the Amazon Live platform, unlocking new dimensions for analytics and ML. - Produce structured, ML-ready datasets that feed Applied Scientists' models and serve features to downstream ranking and personalization systems. - Own and advance data quality: proactive monitoring and anomaly detection so the team stays ahead of issues. - Advance platform engineering maturity — CI/CD for ETL (BDT/Maestro), standardized deployment, and AI-assisted code generation and review. - Partner with Applied Scientists, MLEs, DEs, and the BIE to align data assets to model, serving, and reporting needs. A day in the life You will move fast across a broad surface. Some weeks you will be designing a denormalized content metadata asset with an Applied Scientist to unblock a new model; other weeks you will be integrating a retail or advertising data source, hardening a pipeline's CI/CD, building data-quality alarms, or packaging features for the distribution team's ranking systems. You will partner daily with scientists, MLEs, DEs, and the BIE — scoping what to build and how it will be consumed — and you will have self-serve analytics agents and agentic operational tooling to accelerate your work (and a hand in extending that tooling as the platform grows). The pace is quick, the problems span the full data lifecycle, and the ownership is real. About the team The DESA team owns the data platform, analytics, and sciences for Amazon Live and Shop the Show. It is a compact, senior, high-trust team: DEs own the infrastructure and foundational data assets, the BIE owns executive reporting, Applied Scientists and MLEs own the models, experiments, and signals that turn data into product value, and everyone collaborates closely across those boundaries. As a Data Engineer here, you own forward-looking data architecture — the durable, reusable foundation the intelligence layer is built on — and you get exposure to the entire data domain, from event ingestion through production ML and leadership reporting. Your datasets become shared org infrastructure: the inputs to attribution models for partner teams, ranking features for distribution, and the reporting the business runs on. - 3+ years of data engineering experience - Experience with data modeling, warehousing and building ETL pipelines - Experience with SQL - Experience with AWS technologies like Redshift, S3, AWS Glue, EMR, Kinesis, FireHose, Lambda, and IAM roles and permissions - Experience with non-relational databases / data stores (object storage, document or key-value stores, graph databases, column-family databases) Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, STRADA
jobs.description: AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help. You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion. The Service Transformation and Deployment Automation team aims to remove all manual touchpoints from service operations within Amazon Web Services (AWS) Networking, one of the world’s largest and most complex networks. Software Development Engineers are instrumental in discovering innovative ways to automate and scale services. They drive stability, consistency, and sustainability of the network while never losing sight of the high security bar our customer’s demand. We own a container compute platform in the border network, network device access and locality software, and a business intelligence platform for providing insights into service maturity. This position is located in Minneapolis, USA and working in the heart of AWS global network. Millions of customers rely on Amazon’s network for using our retail websites, accessing content on their Kindles, and building applications and businesses on top of the Amazon Web Services (AWS) Cloud. Our goal is to become The Infrastructure Platform for the world – achieving this goal requires automated and massively scalable software services. Success depends on our world-class network infrastructure, and our network depends on our automation. This position involves on-call responsibilities, typically for one week every two months. We don’t like getting paged in the middle of the night or on the weekend, so we work to ensure that our systems are fault tolerant. When we do get paged, we work together to resolve the root cause so that we don’t get paged for the same issue twice. Our team is dedicated to supporting new team members. Our team has a broad mix of experience levels and Amazon tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing and mentorship. Our senior engineers truly enjoy mentoring more junior engineers and engineers from non-traditional backgrounds through one-on-one mentoring and thorough, but kind, code reviews. We care about your career growth. We try to assign projects and tasks based on what will help each team member develop into a better-rounded engineer and enable them to take on more complex tasks in the future. Key job responsibilities You will be responsible for the design, implementation and quality of services you deliver. Your experience working in software development or in an enterprise environment will help us implement automated solutions across a variety of applications and systems. You’ll also: • Design, implement, test, deploy and maintain innovative solutions to transform service performance, durability, cost, and security. • Write high quality distributed system software. • Work in an agile, startup-like development environment, where you are always working on the most important stuff. • Work closely with our Network/Systems/Software Engineering teams to ensure fast and smooth roll-out of new designs and products, as well as assist with deployment and sustaining of networking software tools. • Use data to measure success and take responsibility for the quality of your service and, regardless of their source, strive to prevent faults from impacting your customers. • Use your strong problem-solving skills, ability to understand and scope solutions, work across teams to drive solutions. • Contribute to documentation of process and procedures. • Learn from others and help grow those in your team to achieve their best. • Take ownership, consider tradeoffs and lean on your expertise to ensure the job gets done. • Participate in an on-call rotation with your team. A day in the life Engineers in the Backbone Enterprise and Regional Engineering (BERE) organization have a wide range of responsibilities; we work with internal partners to develop and implement the next-generation platforms along with the tooling ecosystems to support these platforms driving efficiency and scalability through the automation of builds, configuration deployment, and the scaling of capacity. As our network is one of the largest in the world, there is no blueprint allowing our engineers to develop solutions to complex challenges that we face daily. We encourage durable solutions that look around corners while taking into consideration our customer needs from a cost, performance, and reliability perspective. Our team develops tooling that provides the required visibility and control of traffic across the network, while prioritizing the automatic mitigation of events to minimize the impact to our customers during events. In this role you: • Work in a 24x7 team on-call rotation, with ability to drive into workplace for critical events/needs. • Manage customers during problem resolution and operating efficiently under pressure. • Sit at the computer during scheduled work hours with appropriate breaks while maintaining a high level of alertness and attention to detail. • Travel to data center/network sites and Amazon/customer offices as needed. About the team Within AWS Networking, the Backbone Enterprise, and Regional Engineering (BERE) organization is responsible for the design, implementation, and operations of a wide array of networking infrastructure that provide global connectivity between all AWS Regions and edge locations. BERE provides the massive scale required to support our AWS customers and internal services, via a network that experiences 70% growth annually. In addition, they have teams that are responsible for the design and operation of our global corporate office and Data Center network, allowing tens of thousands of Amazonians to perform their daily tasks in support of our customers. AWS Global Connectivity and Network Availability (GCNA) Videos: • Working at AWS in the GCNA Team - Meet Robert, VP: https://youtu.be/8v5i42FL02w • Working at AWS in the GCNA Team - Meet Xiaonan, Sr. Systems Development Engineer: https://youtu.be/58Q1SyGZ4qg *Why AWS* Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses. *Diverse Experiences* Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying. *Work/Life Balance* We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud. *Inclusive Team Culture* Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness. *Mentorship and Career Growth* We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional. - 5+ years of non-internship professional software development experience - 5+ years of programming with at least one software programming language experience - 5+ years of leading design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience - Experience as a mentor, tech lead or leading an engineering team - 5+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience - Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, AWS Security Communications
jobs.description: AWS Security's Security Communications (SecComms) team builds and operates the platforms, tools, and systems that enable Amazon's security organization to communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders at scale. We support security events, ongoing security programs, vulnerability communications, and strategic initiatives that span multiple Amazon business units and AWS services. Our engineering products are the connective tissue between security findings, remediation owners, and the people responsible for keeping Amazon and its customers safe. We are seeking a senior Software Development Engineer to lead the design, development, and operation of software systems that power security communications workflows, automation, and integrations at scale. This role is for a technical leader who brings engineering rigor to ambiguous problems where the business need is understood but the technology strategy is not yet defined, who owns outcomes across system boundaries, and who thrives working across organizational boundaries with security engineers, program managers, and communications professionals. You will own the architectural direction of the SecComms platform, lead projects staffed by multiple engineers, and act as a force multiplier for the team. Security Communications serves as the engineering and operations hub for AWS-related security messaging, stakeholder notification, and communications tooling across the organization. Our team is responsible for building scalable platforms that enable consistent, reliable, and timely communication during high-severity security events, coordinated vulnerability disclosure, and routine security program operations. We are a cross-functional team - engineers work shoulder-to-shoulder with communications professionals, security operations personnel, AWS service owners, and executives. Candidates should be comfortable leading discussions and building consensus in this environment across both technical and non-technical domains. Operational Excellence • Lead ongoing operational support for the team with appropriate alarms, telemetry, runbooks, and on-call response; effectively prioritize trade-offs between operational improvements and other work. • Drive resolution of the root causes of operational issues and address systemic issues that reduce support costs across the team's services. • Take the lead in identifying and solving architecture deficiencies and areas where software bottlenecks innovation, including in systems you depend on but do not own. • Ensure software failures are addressed with permanent fixes that prevent recurring incidents. Collaboration & Cross-Functional Partnership • Partner with security engineers, program managers, communications leads, and adjacent teams to understand the business and customer value of the team's software, and influence the roadmaps and technical decisions of teams you depend on but don't control. • Build consensus and make an inclusive space for differing views when integrations, dependencies, or shared priorities arise across organizational boundaries. • Make effective priority trade-offs between feature development and operational work, prioritizing long-term results - software quality, business requirements, customer experience, and maintainability - across your team's and related teams' products. • Communicate technical designs and decisions clearly in writing to both technical audiences and to non-technical stakeholders and leadership. Mentorship & Engineering Culture • Actively coach or mentor multiple engineers, on your team and beyond; serve as someone members of other teams seek out for expertise. • Drive adoption of engineering best practices across the team; train new team members on how the SecComms software is constructed, tested, operated, and secured, and how it fits into the broader Amazon Security architecture. • Own and maintain documentation of what the team's software does, how it is built, and how it connects to the bigger picture; keep it current as systems evolve. • Seek diverse perspectives and feedback early, and proactively identify and drive adoption of industry innovations including new tools, design patterns, and AWS capabilities to ensure the team's skills keep pace. jobs.description: Come build the future of data streaming with the Amazon Managed Streaming for Kafka (MSK) team! We are seeking builders for our Amazon MSK service, a fully managed service that makes it easy for customers to build and run applications that use Apache Kafka to process streaming data. We are looking for engineers who are enthusiastic about data streaming, and are as passionate about contributing to open source as they are about solving real customers' business needs, at AWS scale. As a member of the Amazon MSK team, you will be making contributions to the entire core data plane stack that make up the MSK service, the core Kafka platform, and stand-alone tools that make it easier for Kafka community to operate Kafka better. Upstream compatibility is a core tenet of MSK. Your code changes to the Kafka platform will be released back to open source. As a member of an AWS service that builds on top of a popular open source technology, this is a unique opportunity to work on a team that straddles both worlds – open source and Amazon-internal software. You will design and build new features, make performance improvements, identify and investigate new technologies, prototype solutions, build scalable services, and test and review changes, to deliver an exceptional customer experience. The ideal candidate has experience designing large-scale systems supporting millions of transactions per second, enjoys solving complex software problems, and possesses analytical, design and problem-solving skills. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, AWS Transform
jobs.description: With roughly seven out of eight enterprise workloads still running on-premises or on mainframe, the opportunity to help the world's largest organizations move to the cloud is enormous. AWS Transform is building a platform that combines AI-driven automation with deep infrastructure and software engineering to analyze, plan, and execute large-scale application migrations. As a Software Development Engineer on this team, you will work across the full stack, from designing the distributed systems and services that power migration workflows to building the intelligent agents that reason about complex legacy environments. You will own the design and delivery of features and components, from understanding customer needs through implementation, testing, and production operations. You will work with senior engineers on system design, write high-quality, well-tested code, and help operate the services you build. Your work will directly shape how enterprises move their most critical workloads to AWS. You will collaborate closely with senior engineers, product managers, and customer-facing teams to make sure what you build turns into real customer outcomes. If you are excited about solving hard, high-impact problems with strong engineering fundamentals and applied AI skills, we would love to hear from you. Drive the end-to-end design of the features you own, making trade-offs across scalability, performance, and security, and communicate across teams to influence architectural decisions on shared interfaces and infrastructure. Write well-documented, production-quality code that sets an example for others, and make sure solutions are testable and easy for others to extend. Play a key technical role on the team in aligning engineering work with customer needs, turning requirements into product features and delivering them incrementally. Mentor teammates through design and code reviews, foster engineering best practices, and take part in interviewing and recruiting. After working through the details with a senior engineer, you shift to writing and reviewing code, working on infrastructure plumbing one hour and refining an agent's decision logic the next. In the afternoon you meet with your product manager and a customer-facing teammate to go over feedback from an enterprise customer pilot and turn it into improvements for your feature. You wrap up by updating operational dashboards and tuning alerts for a service you helped launch. About the team AWS Transform sits within the Agentic AI organization at Amazon Web Services and is focused on building the next generation of autonomous migration services. The team partners closely with go-to-market, professional services, and enterprise customers to turn complex modernization challenges into repeatable, well-engineered solutions that blend systems infrastructure with applied AI. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, SoC HAL
jobs.description: Description Annapurna Labs builds the custom silicon at the heart of AWS machine learning servers, and we are hiring a software engineer to help build the Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL) that brings these chips to life. If you love working where hardware meets software, writing the code that boots, configures, and debugs some of the largest custom silicon in the world, this is your team. As a Software Engineer on the SoC HAL team, you will write and test C++ for the driver stack across the hardware blocks that make up our chips, learn how the silicon works from the engineers who design it, and grow your skills on a small, fast-moving team inside a large organization. No machine learning background is required (you will pick up ML concepts from colleagues if you want to). This role is based in Cupertino, CA. Key job responsibilities Implement, test, and maintain HAL/driver features for individual hardware blocks (for example PCIe, DDR / HBM memory, DMA, system fabric, interrupt controllers, and boot / firmware), working from designs and interfaces set by more senior engineers. Write clean, well-tested C++ and contribute to the team's test, code-review, and continuous-deployment practices. Debug failures that span software and silicon, with support from the team, and build an understanding of how the HAL interacts with the hardware underneath it. Learn the hardware/software interface by partnering with RTL and design verification engineers on well-scoped questions. Provide feature additions and bug fixes on current and prior chips. A day in the life A typical day moves between writing and reviewing C++ for the HAL, pairing with a teammate on a tricky bug, and learning how a hardware block works from its spec or from the engineer who designed it. You might add a feature to a driver, write tests for it, and work through code-review feedback, then dig into a failure that spans software and silicon. Your teammates are the HAL engineers you build alongside; the hardware design, verification, and firmware teams are close partners you will learn from; and your customers are the internal software teams that rely on the HAL to boot, configure, and debug the chip. About the team Annapurna Labs designs and deploys some of the largest custom silicon in the world, including the Trainium and Inferentia machine learning accelerators. Our SoC HAL team builds the low-level software that boots, configures, and manages these chips, sitting between the hardware and the system software that runs the server. We are a small team that works closely with hardware, holds a high engineering bar, and invests in helping engineers grow. Based in Cupertino, CA, we value mentorship, clear written design, and software that outlasts any single chip. - Knowledge of programming languages such as C/C++, Python, Java or Perl - Experience (non-internship) in professional software development, or currently enrolled in or recently completed a Bachelor's or Master's degree in computer science or a related field - Experience with data structures, algorithms, and software design fundamentals - Bachelor's degree or above in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related fields at time of application - Coursework, internship, or project experience in computer architecture or operating systems - Experience with C or C++ and object-oriented design - Exposure to low-level, embedded, or hardware-adjacent programming - Familiarity with testing, debugging, source control, and build processes in a team setting Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Leo Antenna Team
jobs.description: Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity. The Leo Antenna team is looking for a Software Development Engineer who is excited to work at the intersection of large-scale data systems, Amazon Web Services cloud services, data analysis, and radio frequency hardware. In this role, you will design and build Customer Terminal Fleet Health, the system that keeps a daily hardware health record for every customer terminal Leo operates and flags terminals whose hardware is starting to fail. You will turn telemetry from millions of satellite contacts a day into clear, trustworthy signals that tell engineers which terminals need attention and why. You do not need to come in as a radio frequency expert, but you should have a strong software engineering foundation, experience building data pipelines on Amazon Web Services, a high learning velocity, and the drive to understand phased array antennas, satellite links, and how hardware failures show up in telemetry. This is an individual contributor software development role for someone who enjoys ambiguous technical problems, can learn across disciplines, and wants to build data systems that directly improve the reliability of a satellite network. Export Control Requirement Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. Key job responsibilities Design and build data pipelines on AWS (Step Functions, Athena, Glue, Iceberg, Lambda, S3) that process daily telemetry for the full fleet of customer terminals. Define and own the data model for fleet health: daily per-terminal aggregates, per-satellite views, and the history engineers use to investigate a single terminal. Partner with RF and antenna engineers to understand signal quality, temperature, reboot, and link metrics well enough to separate hardware failures from network, weather, and satellite effects. Develop and validate the rules and models that flag failing hardware, and measure how well they work against terminals returned for repair. Build infrastructure as code with AWS CDK, with deployment pipelines, monitoring, alarms, and integration tests that keep the system reliable. Build dashboards and tools that let engineering and operations teams explore fleet health, compare groups of terminals, and track the effect of software and hardware changes. Apply strong security and data-handling practices to sensitive customer and device data, including least-privilege access, encryption, and privacy controls. Collaborate with data platform and customer terminal software teams to onboard new data sources and improve the telemetry the system depends on. Write high-quality, maintainable code and documentation that other engineers and teams across Leo can build on. A day in the life You may start the day reviewing the overnight fleet health run, checking that every data source arrived and looking at which terminals were newly flagged. You might then sit down with antenna and radio frequency engineers on a group of terminals whose signal quality dropped, digging through the data together to decide whether it points to failing hardware, a software release, or something outside the terminal. Later, you may meet with the data platform and customer terminal software teams to onboard a new telemetry source, then write the infrastructure and pipeline code that brings it into the daily run with tests and alarms in place. You might finish the day with field operations, comparing the watch list against recent hardware returns to see which failures the system flagged early, which it missed, and what each returned terminal can teach the rules. Across all of it, your work helps engineers spot failing hardware before customers notice and measure the effect of software and hardware changes across the fleet. This role requires curiosity, technical depth, and the ability to move between data engineering, cloud infrastructure, and hardware context. You will not just write code; you will help define how Leo understands the health of every terminal in its fleet. About the team The Leo Customer Terminal Software Team supports the devices that connect customers to the Leo satellite network. We provide embedded application software and the underlying Linux system software for these terminals. We work hand in hand with hardware, product, and operations teams to deliver a great experience for our customers. As Leo moves toward full-scale production and global deployment, this is a compelling time to join and help shape how millions of people get online for the first time. - 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience - 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience - 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience - 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience - 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience - Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field - Experience programming with at least one software programming language - 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience - Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, AIO Visualization and Reporting
jobs.description: Join a team that builds the experiences every AWS customer uses to understand, monitor, and optimize what they spend, from individual developers to enterprise FinOps teams managing tens of millions of dollars in monthly spend. The AWS Billing Console Platform team owns the console's hosting platform, on which around thirty AWS engineering teams build their console pages; over fifty customer-facing billing and cost pages of its own; and the rendering engine that turns an AI agent's cost data into the charts, tables and reports customers see. Two AWS agents answer cost questions today, a FinOps agent and Amazon Q in the console, and chatbots and console pages form one ecosystem customers navigate between to get problems solved and questions answered. Today each renders its answers its own way, and a cost figure has to be right the first time. This team is building the rendering layer both agents will draw on: an engine that checks every plotted value against the data the agent gathered, an open artifact format any agent host can render, and the component catalog that makes a cost chart look the same wherever it appears. In the afternoon you pair with an applied scientist on the evaluation set for the next release and sketch the components a new chart needs. Across the week you balance net-new rendering and platform work against the operational excellence that billing customers depend on, and rotate through on-call. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer - Network Observability, Leo Networking Software
jobs.description: Amazon Leo is Amazon’s Low Earth Orbit satellite network, with a mission to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will connect people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity. The Leo Network Observability, Visibility & Analytics team builds the systems that provide deep, end-to-end insight into the health, performance, and reliability of this global telecom network. Our systems span the full Leo service—from satellites and customer terminals to ground gateways, cloud services, and terrestrial network infrastructure—and enable engineers to understand network behavior, rapidly detect failures, and diagnose complex issues across space and ground infrastructure. We are looking for a talented Software Development Engineer II to design, build, and operate network observability and analytics solutions for an advanced global telecommunications service spanning both space and terrestrial networks. As a software engineer on this team, you will build high-scale systems that transform telemetry, network events, traces, and operational signals into actionable visibility. You will work across distributed systems, networking, data pipelines, real-time analytics, and visualization to answer critical questions such as: Is the network healthy? Where is a failure occurring? What is its customer impact? And how quickly can we identify and resolve it? You will collaborate closely with network engineers, scientists, and software engineers to develop novel mechanisms for end-to-end network visibility and diagnostics. Your work will help establish the observability foundations required to operate a highly distributed telecom network where failures can span satellites, beams, customer terminals, gateways, cloud services, and terrestrial infrastructure. Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. Key job responsibilities - Design and develop highly scalable network observability, telemetry, and analytics systems spanning space and terrestrial infrastructure. - Build real-time and near-real-time pipelines that ingest and correlate high-volume network telemetry, events, traces, and health signals. - Develop algorithms and services that provide end-to-end network visibility, including failure detection, localization, correlation, and impact analysis. - Build tools and platforms that enable engineers to quickly understand network health and diagnose complex, multi-hop failures. - Design distributed systems capable of processing large volumes of telemetry while maintaining high availability, durability, and low latency. - Develop APIs, services, dashboards, and analytical tools that expose network health and operational insights to internal customers. - Work closely with network engineers and scientists to translate complex networking problems into robust software solutions. - Establish metrics, service-level indicators, and automated detection mechanisms for critical Leo network components. - Design systems that remain resilient in the presence of intermittent connectivity, partial failures, delayed telemetry, and unreliable network paths. - Participate in the full software development lifecycle, including architecture, implementation, testing, deployment, operational readiness, and on-call support. - Drive technical decisions across team boundaries and contribute to engineering standards for observability, reliability, and operational excellence. - Mentor other engineers and contribute to a culture of high-quality, secure, and maintainable software development. A day in the life You will work on problems at the intersection of distributed systems, networking, telemetry, and large-scale analytics. One day you might design a streaming architecture capable of processing telemetry from millions of network components; another day you might develop a mechanism to identify where packet loss occurred across a multi-hop satellite and terrestrial path. You will work with network engineers and scientists to understand how Leo’s network behaves, develop new ways to make that behavior observable, and turn large volumes of operational data into actionable information. You will also own services in production and work through real operational challenges as the network scales. This role provides opportunities to work across the stack—from telemetry collection on network infrastructure and embedded systems, through distributed data pipelines and analytics, to the APIs and visualization tools used by engineers operating the Leo network. About the team The Leo Network Observability, Visibility & Analytics team is responsible for making a highly distributed global telecom network understandable and operable at scale. We build the visibility layer that connects network signals across satellites, customer terminals, gateways, cloud services, and terrestrial infrastructure. Our systems help transform individual telemetry signals into an end-to-end view of network health, enabling faster detection, diagnosis, and resolution of issues. The problems we solve are inherently distributed and require us to combine software engineering with networking and data science. We are building new capabilities rather than simply applying existing observability patterns to a conventional cloud service. Automation & Standards: Build and maintain automation, standards, reference architectures, and documentation that strengthen deployment consistency and enable teams to consume cloud services safely and consistently. Integration & Collaboration: Engineer and support resilient cloud connectivity, including transit architectures and connectivity between cloud providers and on-premises environments. Observability & Monitoring: Implement and improve observability across cloud services, including metrics, logs, traces, alerting, and capacity dashboards. Stakeholder Support: Advise application and infrastructure teams on cloud, hybrid, and on-premises architecture choices based on reliability, performance, security, and cost. Cost Management: Partner with Finance and Purchasing on cloud cost visibility, forecasting, and commitments, holding yourself accountable for the team's FinOps and efficiency goals. Strong knowledge of cloud networking, including VPCs, routing, DNS, firewalls, load balancing, private connectivity, and interconnect providers. Working knowledge of cloud security fundamentals, including IAM, encryption/key management, secrets management, and least-privilege design. Experience with cloud observability, monitoring, and alerting, and a proven ability to troubleshoot and resolve complex production problems while making sound decisions under pressure. Excellent communication and documentation skills, with the ability to learn quickly, take initiative, and adapt to changing technologies and business needs while working effectively across technical teams and cloud providers. About the Role We're looking for an AI Inference Platform Engineer to build, operate , and optimize the systems that serve large language , vision, multimodal, and embedding models across DRW. This role provides DRW's firmwide interface to modern AI models, from early evaluation through reliable production use . You'll work across inference runtimes, distributed systems, and production platform engineering, with deep GPU literacy. You'll own the serving platform end-to-end: onboarding newly released models, measuring quality and performance equivalence across serving configurations, scheduling workloads across tenants, and continuously improving latency, throughput, utilization, reliability, and cost across the inference fleet. What You'll Do Optimize LLM inference performance across modern NVIDIA GPU architectures and inference runtimes. Build end-to-end performance profiling and observability to identify bottlenecks from individual GPU kernels through multi-node inference systems. Design and optimize KV cache and distributed inference architectures, including caching, routing, memory tiering, and prefill/decode strategies. Own day-0 model onboarding, determining the appropriate runtime, precision, sharding, memory, batching, cache policy, and serving configuration for new models. Maintain validated performance profiles for important model and hardware combinations, including performance and quality regression testing. Measure and monitor quality equivalence across serving configurations, including KV cache quantization, speculative decoding acceptance thresholds, precision choices, and model routing, so in-house serving can be trusted to match reference-model quality on production workloads. Manage the production serving lifecycle of models, including versioning, compatibility, staging, canarying, promotion, rollback, and retirement. Partner with SRE and platform teams to automate model deployment, distribution, production readiness, observability, and reliable operation across environments. Optimize model placement, scaling, and resource allocation across the inference fleet to improve utilization and cost efficiency while meeting performance and reliability requirements. Design and operate multi-tenant scheduling and isolation across shared GPU capacity, balancing latency SLOs, throughput, and priority across concurrent workloads. What We're Looking For The Tech Hands-on experience serving LLMs on NVIDIA GPUs, with familiarity across current and emerging architectures (Hopper, Blackwell, and successors), HBM, Tensor Cores, NVLink / NVSwitch , and the compute and memory bottlenecks that shape serving decisions . Deep expertise in at least one modern inference runtime such as TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, or SGLang. Practical knowledge of inference optimization techniques including continuous batching, scheduling, chunked prefill, speculative decoding, quantization, CUDA Graphs, and paged attention. Understanding of KV cache architecture, including prefix caching, block management, sizing, eviction, quantization, cache-aware routing, and multi-tier caching. Experience measuring model quality equivalence across serving configurations, including evaluation harnesses, task-specific benchmarks, and regression detection for quantization, KV cache, and speculative decoding changes. Experience designing and tuning distributed inference systems, including tensor parallelism, multi-node deployments, and disaggregated prefill and decode. Experience with multi-tenant GPU scheduling, workload isolation, and QoS across concurrent inference workloads. Proficiency with GPU performance and observability tooling such as Nsight, DCGM, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, and Grafana. Strong Linux and systems performance fundamentals, with the ability to diagnose bottlenecks across hardware, drivers, runtimes, networking, and application layers. Production experience with model serving infrastructure, including CI/CD, automated testing, observability, and production readiness. The Intangibles You take a measurement-driven approach to performance optimization. You take ownership of performance problems across hardware, runtime, model, and infrastructure boundaries. You can move quickly and reprioritize as trading needs change, while maintaining a high bar for production systems. You understand the importance of reliability, predictability, and performance when AI systems are integrated into trading workflows and decision-making processes. You can evaluate unfamiliar models, runtimes, and hardware quickly and make sound engineering decisions with limited prior guidance. You communicate clearly and can explain complex performance tradeoffs across engineering teams. The position is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus.
